item.title: Trump to take call on Russia sanctions law in 10 days as India awaits clarity: Sergio Gor
item.description: US President Donald Trump is expected to make a decision within the next 10 days on sanctions provisions that could affect countries buying Russian oil and gas, including India, US Ambassador to India ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump to take call on Russia sanctions law in 10 days as India awaits clarity: Sergio Gor US President Donald Trump is expected to make a decision within the next 10 days on sanctions provisions that could affect countries buying Russian oil and gas, including India, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said. ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 11:08 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 11:08 IST

US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump is expected to make a decision within the next 10 days on sanctions provisions that could affect countries buying Russian oil and gas, including India, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy forum, the US Envoy said, “He has to make a determination in the next I believe 10 or so days,” Gor said, noting that the President had not imposed sanctions on any country under the law so far and was required to make a determination within 30 days of its passage. Gor added that the legislation passed by the US Congress gives the President authority to impose sanctions on countries involved in buying Russian oil and gas or helping evade sanctions, but stressed that the measures were not directed at any particular country. “The goal is not to punish anyone. The goal is to try to bring an end to this war,” Gor said, adding that Trump was expected to make a determination over the next few days. Gor noted that the legislation had received overwhelming bipartisan support in the US Senate, securing 86 votes out of 100. “I do think the President will make a determination on that over the next few days,” he said. Gor added that the administration understood that countries could not immediately stop their energy supplies, but wanted to work with partners to gradually reduce funds flowing towards the war. Asked whether India could receive sanctions relief or exemptions, Gor said the decision rested with the President. The Ambassador also expressed confidence that India and the US would conclude a trade deal, saying the two sides had made substantial progress despite the complexity of the negotiations. “The big picture, the big framework, the big items are done,” Gor said, adding that the remaining issues included smaller details and new concerns that could emerge as negotiations progressed. He said the negotiations had been underway for around a year and a half and were moving at an unusually fast pace compared with other trade agreements. Gor said the administration had to revisit parts of the earlier trade arrangement after the US Supreme Court ruled the law underpinning it unconstitutional. He added that the US was keen to expand business cooperation with India across sectors, including defence, information technology, data centres and chip manufacturing. Gor further said investment by US companies in India could also support job creation in the United States. Gor said India was well positioned to emerge as a major hub for artificial intelligence (AI) development, with partnerships between Indian firms and leading US technology companies offering benefits to both countries. He said developing AI capabilities on Indian soil, while working with US companies, could strengthen technology cooperation and create opportunities for businesses in both countries. “India would be an incredible fit for AI, for tech development right here on their own soil, but partnering with some of our best companies is a win-win situation,” he said. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Anthropic's Q3 revenue jumps 45% to USD 16.8 billion ahead of anticipated IPO Artificial intelligence company Anthropic's revenue surged 45 per cent to USD 16.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 from the previous quarter, while the company also reported an adjusted profit, reports Reuters.  ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 09:34 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 09:34 IST

Anthropic Logo (Photo/Anthropic). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Artificial intelligence company Anthropic's revenue surged 45 per cent to USD 16.8 billion in the third quarter of 2026 from the previous quarter, while the company also reported an adjusted profit, reports Reuters. The figures were shared with prospective investors at a meeting held at Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters on Wednesday ahead of its anticipated initial public offering (IPO). The revenue rose from USD 11.6 billion in the second quarter and USD 4.7 billion in the first quarter, people who attended the investor meeting said, as per the report. Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao met prospective investors at the event, with some attendees expressing optimism about the company's rapid revenue growth and path to profitability, Reuters reported. The company is targeting a valuation of more than USD 2 trillion for its anticipated IPO, according to the report. Its public-market debut is expected to precede that of rival OpenAI, although the listing could take place after the November US midterm elections. Anthropic is seeking to convince investors that its rapid revenue growth can eventually outweigh the substantial costs of developing and operating increasingly powerful AI systems. According to estimates from analysts who met company executives earlier this week, Anthropic's annual revenue run rate could reach USD 110 billion by the end of 2026. The financial performance comes as AI companies face greater scrutiny over spending on chips, data centres and computing infrastructure. Anthropic has committed at least USD 518 billion over a decade towards cloud services, computing and infrastructure. Last year, the company's revenue increased twelvefold to nearly USD 4.6 billion, even as it recorded an operating loss of more than USD 8 billion, excluding writedowns of liabilities largely linked to previous fundraising. At Wednesday's meeting, Amodei reiterated the company's focus on AI safety but did not discuss threats of human extinction, one attendee told Reuters. This contrasted with the company's prospectus, which warned that advanced AI could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”. Anthropic, founded by former OpenAI executives, develops the Claude family of AI models and has expanded with support from Alphabet's Google and Amazon, which are investors, computing providers and distribution partners, as well as competitors in the AI market. (ANI)

item.title: "Largest offtake agreement in history": Trump announces Taiwan’s upto $80 billion commitment for Alaska LNG
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday (local time) announced that Taiwan had agreed to an offtake commitment worth between USD 70 billion and 80 billion for the Alaska liquefied natural gas (LNG) ...
item.content:encoded:
"Largest offtake agreement in history": Trump announces Taiwan’s upto $80 billion commitment for Alaska LNG US President Donald Trump on Wednesday (local time) announced that Taiwan had agreed to an offtake commitment worth between USD 70 billion and 80 billion for the Alaska liquefied natural gas (LNG) project over the next 20 years, along with a USD 4.4 billion equity investment, while citing South Korea’s USD 50 billion investment in the project. ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 09:28 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 09:28 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday (local time) announced that Taiwan had agreed to an offtake commitment worth between USD 70 billion and 80 billion for the Alaska liquefied natural gas (LNG) project over the next 20 years, along with a USD 4.4 billion equity investment, while citing South Korea’s USD 50 billion investment in the project. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, “I was just in Alaska launching the largest Energy Infrastructure Project in Alaska History--The Alaska LNG Project. This 50 billion-dollar infrastructure investment from the Republic of Korea is part of their Trade and Investment Deal with me.” He added, “I am also announcing today that my Commerce Secretary, Howard Lutnick, has secured an Offtake Commitment from Taiwan of between 70 to 80 Billion Dollars for Alaska LNG — That is 30% of the Pipeline for the next 20 years. This is the largest Offtake Agreement in History.” Trump further said, “On top of that, Taiwan has also agreed to invest 4.4 Billion Dollars in Equity into the Project, because this is now a US Federal Government Project, with all necessary permits secured, and all necessary authorisations delivered, and ready to go.” “This is the Greatest Project in Alaska History, and this only happens with me in the White House. Thank you for your attention to this matter,” he added. However, Taiwan's specific investment arrangements are still subject to further negotiations and commercial agreements. According to Taipei Times, Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs said state-owned CPC Corp, Taiwan, would purchase six million tonnes of Alaska LNG annually once production begins, in line with a letter of intent signed in March last year. The ministry added that CPC would invest in the project's development, including the construction of a 1,299-km pipeline. The ministry said deliveries to Taiwan could begin as early as 2032 if the project starts operations on schedule. It did not confirm whether it had signed a binding sale-and-purchase agreement. “Specific investment arrangements, equity stakes and related terms will be determined through subsequent negotiations and commercial contract procedures,” the ministry said, according to Taipei Times. The ministry said the partnership was expected to diversify Taiwan's LNG supplies, provide greater flexibility in managing supply and distribution, strengthen energy security and deepen ties with the United States. The project's location would allow LNG to be shipped directly to Taiwan across the Pacific Ocean, providing an alternative route to help mitigate geopolitical risks. The Alaska LNG project is expected to produce 20 million tonnes of LNG annually, transporting natural gas from Alaska's North Slope through a pipeline to an export terminal in the state's south. Its developers aim to take a final investment decision on the pipeline by the end of this year, followed by the export facility next year, with initial LNG exports targeted for 2031. According to Taipei Times, the project has secured agreements covering 13 million tonnes annually from buyers in Asia and French energy company TotalEnergies. It needs commitments for another three million tonnes and must convert the agreements into binding deals to secure financing. Earlier in October, Trump warned South Korea that the cost of participating in the Alaska pipeline project could rise if Seoul did not commit soon, after being informed that the country was still studying the proposal. “Tell ’em if they don’t sign shortly, I’m going to double it up. Okay?” Trump told reporters at the White House before boarding Marine One. When asked whether he had announced South Korea's participation prematurely, Trump said, “Well, I didn’t jump the gun. I mean, they were there and, uh, they were represented, and let’s see. If they don’t wanna do it, that’s okay with me.” “I’ll just charge ’em more,” he added. (ANI)

item.description: Highlighting recent high-level diplomatic contact, he added, "We had a summit-level meeting when President Xi was here for the BRICS Summit; he met with our Prime Minister." ...
item.content:encoded:
MEA highlights sustained India-China diplomatic talks as Piyush Goyal's signals scope for renewed engagement Highlighting recent high-level diplomatic contact, he added, "We had a summit-level meeting when President Xi was here for the BRICS Summit; he met with our Prime Minister." ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 09:25 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 09:25 IST

MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Ministry of External Affairs on Wednesday reflected on the series of high-level diplomatic interactions already underway between India and China, as Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal’s signalled scope for rebuilding economic ties with Beijing. When asked about potential plans for bilateral meetings and the scope of closer cooperation envisioned by Goyal’s comments, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal emphasised that the diplomatic channel has seen continuous dialogue over the past year. "On India-China relations, we have had a series of meetings over the last year or so," Jaiswal stated during the media briefing. Highlighting recent high-level diplomatic contact, he added, "We had a summit-level meeting when President Xi was here for the BRICS Summit; he met with our Prime Minister." "We have continued to keep you informed of the developments in this relationship, and we will continue to do so as we go ahead," he added. His remarks come as Piyush Goyal said that India is open to business engagements with countries across the world, including China, provided the terms are fair, and the geopolitical situation remains stable, signalling scope for renewed economic engagement with Beijing. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, “We are open to all countries around the world as long as we get a fair deal, as long as we are ensured continuity in the engagement, and as long as the geopolitical situation does not deteriorate,” Goyal said during a panel discussion on supply-chain resilience and technology partnerships. “We are working to develop the relation with China once again, but the last word has not yet been scripted on this journey,” he added. Meanwhile, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said peace and tranquillity in the border areas were essential to normalising India-China relations, stressing that any disturbance along the border would have consequences. Speaking in a conversation with John Micklethwait, Editor-in-Chief of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in Delhi, Jaishankar said India and China have no agreed border and that the issue has persisted for decades. "We don't have an agreed border between India and China. This is not a new issue; it's been going on for multiple decades... From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said. Emphasising India's position on normalising ties with China, Jaishankar said the boundary situation had to remain stable for broader bilateral relations to progress. "The point we make to the Chinese is: 'If you want a normal relationship, if the rest of the relationship is to move, it's common sense. It's a no-brainer that the boundary has to be stable, that we need peace and tranquillity in the border areas.' As the border areas are settling down, they have settled down to a great extent since 2024; the relationship is commensurately moving towards normalcy," he said. On whether India would consider allowing greater Chinese investment if an early harvest agreement were reached, the External Affairs Minister said discussions on the possibilities were ongoing, while clarifying that investment and market access policies would be addressed separately from the boundary issue. (ANI)
